results.title: OAuth 2.0
results.snippet:
Ramp API uses the [OAuth 2.0 protocol](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749) to handle authorization and access control. Currently Ramp supports two grant types -- Client Credentials and Authorization Code.

Authorization Code Grant
There are three parties involved in the `Authorization Code` -- the client (your application), the server (Ramp) and the user (data owner);
As an overview, the flow has the following steps
1. Your application sends the user to authenticate with Ramp
2. The user sees the authorization prompt and approves the app’s request for data access
3. The user is redirected back via a `redirect_uri` with a temporary `authorization code`
4. Your application exchanges the `authorization code` for an `access token`
5. Ramp verifies the params and returns the `access_token`
6. You application gets a new `access_token` with the `refresh_token`
Now let's walkthrough all the steps

| Grant Type | Use Case | User Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |

| **Refresh Token** | Renew access after an Authorization Code grant | None after the initial authorization |

results.snippet:
## 1. Create your app and get credentials
First, you'll need to create a developer app to get your API credentials.
1. In your Ramp account, go to **Company → Developer** (you'll need admin access).
2. Click **Create New App**.
3. Name your app (e.g., "API Quickstart") and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types**, click **Add new grant type** → select **Client Credentials**.
5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select `transactions:read`.
6. Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**. Store them securely – you'll need them in the next step.
For more details on authorization, see the [Authorization Guide](</developer-api/v1/authorization>).
## 2. Get an access token
With your credentials, request an access token. Ramp authenticates this `/developer/v1/token` request with HTTP Basic Auth: base64-encode `client_id:client_secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header. The token authenticates your API requests.
Replace `{environment-url}` with:
- `https://demo-api.ramp.com` for Sandbox
- `https://api.ramp.com` for Production

results.title: Ramp Help Center
results.snippet:
Ramp [provides an API](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/overview/getting-started) to programmatically access data and take action. The Ramp API uses an OAuth 2.0 flow to generate credentials to auth against the Ramp API. The OAuth 2.0 flow generates a client ID, client secret, access token(s), and refresh token(s). You can find documentation for the OAuth 2.0 flow for the Ramp API [here](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/authorization).

A client secret is a private key that’s generated for your app to authenticate against the API in conjunction with the client ID. Because the client secret is a private credential that’s used to authenticate your app, if a client secret is leaked it should be rotated in the app settings page.
Follow these steps to rotate a client secret. You need a role with permissions to view the Developer Console and manage Ramp API settings to see these options.
1. Go to [app.ramp.com](https://app.ramp.com/) . On the left-hand sidebar, click on “Company” > “Developer”.
2. Click the name of the app whose secret leaked to open the configuration menu.

results.title: Ramp Help Center
results.snippet:
Ramp’s Developer API allows teams to programmatically access Ramp data and build automations or integrations tailored to their workflows. It provides secure, scoped access to objects like transactions, cards, users, and more.

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.
Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for

1. Open [Developer apps](https://app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer/apps) in Ramp.
2. For your first app, click **Start building**. If you already have an app, click **Create new app**.
3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types**, confirm **Client credentials** is turned on.
5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read`. If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

For apps that access the whole business, an Admin or Business Owner must approve. Other users see "An admin must connect this app." For apps that act as an individual user, an admin must first enable the app for the organization in **Manage Access**.

results.title: How to use Ramp API ?
results.snippet:
Developers access the Ramp API through a straightforward process involving account creation, key generation, and environment selection. Begin by signing up for a [Ramp business account ](https://ramp.com/?ref=apidog.com)if you lack one. Ramp verifies businesses during onboarding, a process that typically spans 1-3 business days.

Ramp structures its API pricing around the broader platform fees, ensuring predictability for developers.

Basic access to the API comes free with any Ramp account. You incur no additional charges for standard endpoints like transactions or cards. However, advanced features—such as custom webhook processing or high-volume data exports—may require enterprise plans.

Free tier supports unlimited projects—download now to complement your Ramp API setup.

results.title: Transactions
results.snippet:
**Transactions**
Card transactions, sorted by most recent `user_transaction_time`. Each transaction links to a user, a card, a merchant, optional receipts, and accounting field selections.
Part of [Cards](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/cards-and-funds). For the relationship to bills, vendors, and accounting fields, see [Data relationships](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/data-relationships).
**Accounting field locations.** Field selections live in two places: the root `accounting_field_selections` array (transaction-wide) and `line_items[i].accounting_field_selections` (splittable fields, even on single-line transactions).
**Looking to:**
- Sync transactions to your ERP? See [ERP Integrations](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/erp-integrations#split-transaction-line-items).
- Get real-time transaction events? See [Webhooks](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/webhooks).
## List transactions
This endpoint supports filtering and ordering. If state is not set, all transactions except declined transactions will be returned. Note that setting multiple ordering parameters is unsupported.
## Query string parameters
Filter transactions by accounting field selection.

results.title: docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/developer-mcp.txt
results.snippet:
Developer MCP is Ramp's unauthenticated Model Context Protocol server for developers building with Ramp's API. It gives AI assistants live access to Ramp's developer documentation, API reference, and OpenAPI schemas directly inside your coding workflow.
Unlike Ramp MCP servers that access account data, Developer MCP does not require a Ramp account, OAuth login, API key, or developer app. It only serves public Ramp Developer API documentation.
Why use Developer MCP?
Developer MCP reads from Ramp's published developer docs and OpenAPI exports, so assistants can look up current guides, endpoint reference material, request bodies, response shapes, and parameter definitions.
Ask for an endpoint by operation ID, docs URL, HTTP method and path, or natural selector. Developer MCP can return the matching OpenAPI operation, including request and response schemas.
Use Developer MCP to answer implementation questions without leaving your editor: authentication setup, pagination, webhooks, required fields, endpoint behavior, and schema details.

Ramp MCP lets you securely connect Ramp with AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Notion.

One-click installation from [Claude's MCP directory](https://claude.ai/directory/61bac03c-3f98-4b3c-affb-1b99533fa82c). Sign in to your Ramp account when prompted.

### Notion
Notion AI can connect to Ramp MCP as an external data source. You can install Ramp from Notion's [connector marketplace](https://www.notion.com/@ramp), or use a custom configuration in Notion's MCP connections settings with the server URL `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. See Notion's documentation for configuring external MCP servers.

results.title: agents.ramp.com/docs/mcp
results.snippet:
Use the [Ramp app](https://app.ramp.com) when a person needs to review context,
handle an exception, or complete work directly. The
[Agent Tools reference](/docs/reference/agent-tools) lists every tool available
in the CLI and MCP.

## Custom MCP clients
Point the client at `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. For the Ramp sandbox
(demo.ramp.com, the same environment as the CLI's `--env sandbox`), use
`https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp`. Clients that read MCP JSON usually expect:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"ramp": {
"url": "https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp"
}
}
}
```
Custom clients and gateways need their exact redirect URI allowlisted before
authorization can complete:
- Use `https://`, or `http://` only with `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`. Ramp also
accepts the `claude://`, `cursor://`, `grokbot://`, and `perplexity-app://`
schemes; other custom schemes are not supported.
- Submit the exact host. Wildcard subdomains are not supported.
- [Request redirect URI access](https://docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/mcp-redirect-whitelist-request)
for the client or gateway.
